De Ville

Dress · 25mm–42mm · Typically 30m, with some models having no specified water resistance. · quartz · 1973–2026

The De Ville family represents Omega's line of elegant and classic dress watches, often characterized by refined aesthetics, slim profiles, and sophisticated movements. Signature design cues include simple dials, slender lugs, and the use of precious metals, though stainless steel models are also common.

The story

Originally introduced as part of the Seamaster line in the early 1960s, the De Ville distinguished itself with a more formal design. By 1967, its popularity led to its launch as a standalone collection, where it became a canvas for Omega's design creativity, winning several awards in the 1970s. The family evolved to include quartz models during the 1980s and was later chosen to debut the revolutionary Co-Axial escapement in 1999, marking a significant technical milestone. In the 21st century, the De Ville has continued to be a platform for innovation with the introduction of in-house Co-Axial calibers and collections like the Hour Vision with its sapphire case sides.
